principles: Fail closed: aliases, help text, and warning copy must never bypass lifecycle gates.
Normalize once: convert aliases to canonical fields before handlers persist or gate evidence.
Phase-aware messaging: user guidance must describe the current phase and the real next recovery path.
Keep B-7fc2 boundary clean: avoid unrelated --json stdout/human hint refactors.
Verify through existing smoke contracts before adding new test surfaces.
drivers: validate storyId currently looks successful yet misses story evidence, which is a gate-evidence correctness issue.
Scope and owner messages are lifecycle UX, but their wording can steer users into wrong phase actions.
Parallel development must not corrupt story metadata or collide with B-7fc2/B-7fc2-like active work.

options.name: minimal-compatible-fixes
pros: Smallest blast radius across CLI schema, verifier normalization, help rendering, and scope copy.
Keeps existing command policies/gates unchanged while making UX honest.
Easy to split among parallel agents and integrate with focused smoke tests.
cons: Leaves broader CLI output consistency to B-7fc2.
Requires careful conflict resolution in cli-engine.ts because validate schema and help rendering share the file.

options.name: broad-cli-contract-refactor
pros: Could centralize all alias/help/output behavior in one framework layer.
cons: Overlaps B-7fc2 JSON stdout contract story.
Higher risk of changing unrelated command behavior and breaking lifecycle gates.

options.name: documentation-only-guidance
pros: Could explain correct commands to users.
cons: Does not fix silent validate storyId evidence miss.
Does not make command help or session_brief output mechanically truthful.

rationale: Choose minimal-compatible-fixes because the defects are concrete lifecycle UX/API mismatches with existing narrow code hooks; broad output refactors belong to B-7fc2 and docs-only would leave gate evidence behavior wrong.

preMortem.scenario: validate storyId alias is accepted for ownership but not normalized for the handler.
preMortem.trigger: Zod strips storyId or both story/storyId are passed with conflicting values.
preMortem.consequence: validate appears to pass while test-evidence remains stale or the wrong story receives evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Add storyId to validate schema, normalize/conflict-check in one place, and test JSON storyId, --story, no-story, and conflict cases.

preMortem.scenario: Scope stale copy becomes too soft and hides a real REVIEW blocker.
preMortem.trigger: Phase-aware message treats REVIEW stale binding like TEST advisory.
preMortem.consequence: REVIEW→TEST could be attempted without fresh reviewer scope binding.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep hard blockers first, retain REVIEW stale/missing instructions, and assert fail/stale/advisory cases in semantic scope smoke.

preMortem.scenario: Owner help advertises takeover for commands where it is irrelevant or unsafe.
preMortem.trigger: Help renderer blindly adds meta flags to every command including read-only commands.
preMortem.consequence: Users infer takeover is required/valid for diagnostic reads and may overuse forceTakeover.
preMortem.mitigation: Derive help meta guidance from command ownership policy/dynamic validate story target semantics and test owner-gated vs read-only help.

preMortem.scenario: Parallel agents conflict or mutate story metadata independently.
preMortem.trigger: Agents run checklist_update/story_advance or work in the canonical worktree concurrently.
preMortem.consequence: Lease churn, stale artifacts, or metadata merge conflicts obscure the actual code fixes.
preMortem.mitigation: Give agents isolated branches/worktrees and explicit instruction to avoid story metadata writes; supervisor performs all Lattice lifecycle operations.

preMortem.scenario: B-a30e accidentally changes machine-readable JSON stdout behavior owned by B-7fc2.
preMortem.trigger: Fixing validate/help copy expands into generic output decoration changes.
preMortem.consequence: Two active stories overlap and regress each other.
preMortem.mitigation: Scope B-a30e to schema normalization, handler persistence, help text, and phase-aware scope messages; no broad stdout formatting refactor.
